items.question: How much cash is actually in hand today, separate from revenue you expect later?
items.purpose: Establishes the only pool affordability may be judged against (rule-cash-is-not-revenue).
items.when_to_ask: At the start of every affordability assessment.

items.question: How much of that cash is already committed, and to what: taxes, payroll, deposits, or existing obligations?
items.purpose: Produces the committed bucket so the available remainder can be computed (rule-available-cash-only).
items.when_to_ask: Immediately after the cash figure, before any option is scored.

items.question: What reserve has to stay untouched for your household and your business to remain stable?
items.purpose: Sets the reserve floor the assessment must protect; a commitment that raids it destabilizes the foundation the owned question guards.
items.when_to_ask: Before judging any commitment that approaches the available amount.

items.question: Is this a one-time amount or a recurring obligation, and if recurring, for how long and at what total?
items.purpose: Separates a single payment from an ongoing drain; recurring costs are judged against monthly free cash, not a single balance.
items.when_to_ask: Whenever an option's cost is quoted as a monthly or periodic figure.

items.question: Does this commitment touch household money in any way, directly or as a backstop?
items.purpose: Surfaces household-fund exposure, a financial_feasibility trigger that requires its own assessment (rule-household-business-separate).
items.when_to_ask: Whenever the funding source is a personal account, a personal guarantee, or unstated.

items.question: If exact figures are not available or you would rather not share them, what ranges can you give for cash on hand and for what is already committed?
items.purpose: Respects a client who declines exact amounts while still permitting a worst-case assessment at lowered evidence strength (rule-minimal-figures-no-manufacture).
items.when_to_ask: When the client declines exact figures or does not know them yet.

items.question: What is the smallest version of this commitment that would still tell you whether it works?
items.purpose: Opens the bounded-test path (rule-smaller-test) when the full commitment fails the available-cash test.
items.when_to_ask: After a full-size option fails or cannot be confirmed affordable.

note: Signature questions for this seat, drawn from the Section 7.5 analysis contract: distinguish cash from revenue, recurring obligations from optional spending, and available reserve from money already committed; ask for the minimal figures needed.
